children: HDFC Bank shares rose over 2 percent in early trade on August 31 as investors weighed the lender’s impending leadership transition. Several brokerages maintained bullish calls despite near-term uncertainty over the appointment of a new MD and CEO. The stock climbed 2.05 percent to Rs 735.1, outperforming a weak broader market. At 9:18 am, the Sensex was down 251 points, or 0.32 percent, at 77,014, while the Nifty 50 fell 111 points to 24,065.

Speculation over a successor has intensified after MD and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan informed the board that he would not seek reappointment and would retire on October 26. HDFC Bank has said its board will fast-track the process of selecting his successor.

Moneycontrol reported that HDFC Bank expects to appoint its new CEO “well before” Jagdishan’s retirement on October 26, with the board potentially considering both internal and external candidates. Reuters has reported that deputy managing director Kaizad Bharucha could be among those considered for the role.

CNBC-TV18, citing sources, reported that HDFC Bank’s board is considering former State Bank of India chairman Dinesh Khara for the MD and CEO position. Khara had earlier been approached for the part-time chairman role at HDFC Bank but declined.

The choice of successor will now be central to the investment case for HDFC Bank, as the new leadership inherits a lender still navigating some of the after-effects of its merger with erstwhile HDFC Ltd, say brokerages.

Bernstein maintained its ‘outperform’ rating on HDFC Bank with a target price of Rs 1,150, implying around 60 percent upside from Friday’s closing price. The brokerage views the leadership transition as a net positive, saying an incoming CEO could provide a natural opportunity to reset the bank’s narrative.

JPMorgan also retained its ‘overweight’ call on the stock with a target price of Rs 990, indicating around 37 percent upside from Friday’s close. The brokerage said the development could weigh on the stock in the near term, but a timely succession could ease the leadership overhang. A revival in net interest income growth remains crucial to restoring investor confidence, it added.

IIFL termed Jagdishan’s decision neutral to modestly positive, arguing that it removes the tail risk of a potentially truncated tenure subject to regulatory approval. While Kaizad Bharucha appears to be a probable internal candidate, IIFL noted that tenure restrictions could limit his runway. A credible external candidate, in contrast, could provide a clean leadership reset and a longer tenure, according to the brokerage.

Other brokerages have taken a more cautious approach to the transition. Jefferies retained its ‘buy’ rating but lowered its target price to Rs 880 from Rs 1,050 and cut its FY27-29 earnings estimates by 3 percent each. It expects the leadership transition to potentially affect revenue momentum, particularly deposit mobilisation and fee income, while heightened uncertainty could raise the bank’s cost of equity and weigh on valuations.
Still, Jefferies said HDFC Bank’s valuation at around 1.5 times one-year forward price-to-book was not demanding enough to warrant a downgrade.

ICICI Securities also maintained its ‘buy’ recommendation but cut its target price to Rs 920 from Rs 1,020. It lowered the target valuation multiple to around 1.8 times from 2 times previously to account for uncertainty surrounding the MD and CEO succession.

Axis Capital was more constructive, maintaining its ‘buy’ call and Rs 1,030 target price. It said Jagdishan’s decision removes concerns over the possibility of a shorter second term and clears the way for a successor who could receive a full three-year tenure.

HDFC Bank shares had closed 1.3 percent higher at Rs 720.30 on August 28. However, the stock has fallen 27.3 percent so far in 2026, substantially underperforming the Nifty 50, which is down 7.5 percent over the same period. The bank’s market capitalisation stands at more than Rs 11.1 lakh crore.

title: HDFC Bank shares jump over 2%, brokerages see CEO transition as potential reset; Bernstein sees 60% upside
